title: SB 214 (2025-2026 Regular Session (first year)): Elections and Primaries; electors to cast physical absentee on-request ballots as an alternative to using other authorized means of casting in-person votes; authorize (legis.ga.gov caption, Senate Journal 2025 p. 2972: "so as to authorize electors to cast physical absentee on-request ballots as an alternative to using other authorized means of casting in-person votes")

(section) As introduced (233014), proposed on-request ballot section, subsection (a); this wording is NOT in the House Rules substitute (search for "identification" finds nothing there)
(quote) (1) If on the date of a primary, election, or runoff, an elector presents himself or herself at the polling place in his or her designated precinct for the purpose of casting a ballot in such primary, election, or runoff; or (2) If during the period of advance voting provided for by subsection (d) of Code Section 21-2-385, an elector presents himself or herself at an absentee polling place, advance voting location, or registration office in his or her county of residence for the purpose of casting a ballot in a primary, election, or runoff and if the elector's name appears on the list of registered electors and he or she has presented proper identification pursuant to Code Section 21-2-417, then such elector shall be entitled to cast an absentee on-request ballot pursuant to this Code section.
(other) House Rules substitute: state provides voting equipment as of January 1, 2028, which may include hand marked paper ballots; ballot on demand printing; definitions; ballot design records; electronic ballot marking devices for voters with disabilities; priority for voters with children aged two or younger; scanners reject overvotes; data posted after polls close; paper-ballot audit pilot; recounts; amends SB 189 (2024) effective date; effective dates
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
